subject: NA/NaN Hessian evaluation with endogenous binary variable

messages.author: 74b4c009a1d479b9
messages.subject: NA/NaN Hessian evaluation with endogenous binary variable
parts:
Dear Experts, 

I am running a pretty large SEM model using lavaan 0.6.11 and I am encountering the following problem. 

Most of my variables are questionnaire items that take values 1-5. I use these items to derive some continuous latent variables using the =~ operator. In my model I also have 2 endogenous binary variables that are predicted by these continuous latent variables and some exogenous variables using the ~ operator. 

So far, I have been running this model with the following command:

mod_fit <- sem(mod, data = bl, estimator='WLSMV', missing='pairwise', orthogonal = TRUE)

If I do this, the model fits the data well and I have no problems. 

However, I would like the fitting to treat my two endogenous binary variables as categorical. If I make the two binary variables categorical with the ordered() command as described in your instructions and then I run the model as above, I get the following error: 

mod_fit <- sem(mod, data = bl, estimator='WLSMV', missing='pairwise', orthogonal = TRUE)

Error in nlminb(start = cache$theta, objective = minObjective, gradient = minGradient,  :
  NA/NaN Hessian evaluation
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, cluster = cluster,  :
  lavaan WARNING: 14 cases were deleted due to missing values in
          exogenous variable(s), while fixed.x = TRUE.
2: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, cluster = cluster,  :
  lavaan WARNING: some cases are empty and will be ignored:
  61 79 101 115 130 185 192 197
3: In sqrt(evar) : NaNs produced
4: In sqrt(evar) : NaNs produced

Would you have any insights into what I might be doing wrong? 

I have noticed that removing "missing='pairwise'" makes the model run, so can one only get listwise deletion when using endogenous categorical variables? 

Thank you very much, 


Leonardo Tozzi
